title: Integration and End-to-End Testing
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of integration and end-to-end testing using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates integration and end-to-end testing.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Integration and End-to-End Testing** as part of **Testing, Debugging, Documentation, and Quality**. Reliable Kotlin code is supported by repeatable tests, meaningful assertions, debuggable failure reports, documentation, and review—not by coverage alone. Use the subtopics—Testing Component Boundaries, Testing Persistence and Network Layers, Stable Test Data and Cleanup—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Professional applications need repeatable tests, clear APIs, dependable dependencies, security checks, and observable failures. Apply this concept in small steps before integrating it into a larger project.

content_blocks.text: Integration and End-to-End Testing removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset
content_blocks.text: If the example fails, first confirm which runtime/project type the snippet requires. Read the first useful compiler or runtime message, check imports and declared dependencies, reduce the example to a minimal case, and rerun. For target-specific code, use the target toolchain rather than assuming a console or browser runner can execute it.
